newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Leighton wins A$90.6 mln HK contract.
newsitem.headline: Leighton wins A$90.6 mln HK contract.

text.p: Leighton Contractors (Asia) Ltd, a subsidiary of Australian construction group Leighton Holdings Ltd, said on Monday it had won a Hong Kong contract to design and construct two aqueducts in a joint venture with Japanese contractor Kumagai Gumi Co Ltd.

The total value of the contract from the Water Supplies Department of the Hong Kong government is HK$1.09 billion (A$181 million) and Leighton's share is HK$545 million (A$90.6 million), the company said.

The contract involves the construction of an 11.9 km steel lined treated water aqueduct and a one km raw water aqueduct between Tai Po and Butterfly Valley as part of the Metropolitan Area and North Eastern New Territories water supply project.
Leighton said the contract also includes site formation works, construction of access roads and mechanical and electrical building services works.
It said work on the aqueducts will commence immediately and the project is scheduled for completion in 2000.
